claims.statement: Postgres service example uses container image postgres, label postgres, example default database credential and health checks. Every service requires image; sample credential/health options are not production-safe configuration or runtime readiness proof.
Hosted runners can reach private registries, secret managers and on-premises resources through private-network configurations; capability is not actual connectivity or universal supported topology.
OIDC tokens can authenticate workflows to external services; authentication alone does not establish a network tunnel, provider trust or resource authorization.
WireGuard on both runner and private service can provide an overlay alternative to separate API Gateway infrastructure. No installation, tunnel keys or route configuration authorized or performed.
Private-fork policy procedure selects Fork pull request workflows options and saves; UI procedure is not target authorization or effective setting verification.

Private fork policy choices separate running read-only/no-secrets workflows, sending write tokens, sending all secrets and approval for collaborators without write by someone with write. Opting into secrets/write is an explicit exception to generic fork withholding, not an approved safe default.

Policies govern private-fork pull_request events: FPT private repositories with organization/repository scope; other branches private/internal with enterprise/organization/repository scope. Not a rule for all PR event types.
Enterprise Actions proxy guidance supports HTTP proxies only, not SOCKS5 or HTTPS proxies. Proxy protocol restriction is distinct from HTTPS target traffic and current target network capability.

Legacy OSSRH example runs Maven batch deploy with MAVEN_USERNAME/MAVEN_PASSWORD sourced from named username/token secrets. No publishing or secrets used; legacy-service caveat in related intro applies.
GitHub Packages example uses Maven batch deploy with repository token environment and permissions key controlling rights. Token presence is not published-package receipt or authorization.
Java publishing guide supports one/multiple registries, but explicitly warns examples refer to Legacy OSSRH and links changed Maven Central publishing. Not a verified current deployment recipe.

Untrusted pull_request_target code risks cache poisoning and unintended write/secrets access; separate safe-use and untrusted-checkout references are required, not implicitly reviewed. This qualifies privileged-event exceptions rather than treating every fork as safe.

Packaged JavaScript should be pure JS without additional binary reliance for Ubuntu/Windows/macOS compatibility. Actions run on runner and may use preinstalled binaries; portable intent is not tested universal architecture support.
Redis client tutorial reads REDIS_HOST/REDIS_PORT set by Connect to Redis step; environment presence is not actual connection or reviewed client source.
Redis service uses container image/label and health options; tag such as redis:6 selects version but is not immutable digest. Service requires image, and no container executed.

Full ref is event-specific: pushed branch/tag, unmerged PR merge ref, merged PR destination, release tag; unavailable if event has no branch/tag. Branch format refs/heads, ordinary unmerged PR refs/pull/number/merge, pull_request_target base branch, tags refs/tags. Never substitute PR head for merge/base automatically.
Short ref name matches displayed branch/tag; unmerged PR format is number/merge, not contributor branch name. Parent event exceptions remain separately reconciled.

ref_protected true indicates protections or feature-conditional rulesets configured for the triggering ref. Configuration signal alone does not prove effective enforcement, bypass coverage or passing required checks.
Ref type accepts branch or tag; missing ref remains event-dependent, not a fabricated branch type.

Authenticated job-container pulls may use credentials map username/password equivalent to docker login values. No credentials retrieved or login executed; required registry access and safe secret storage remain separate.
